Report_ID: Event-free survival (EFS), 3-year rate and EFS events
Title: Impact of 12 weeks nab-paclitaxel + carboplatin or gemcitabine followed by anthracycline administration according to pCR in triple-negative early breast cancer: Survival results of WSG-ADAPT-TN phase II trial
Author: Gluz, Oleg
Comment: This conference abstract reports NO hazard ratio, no 95% CI, and no p-value for the EFS comparison between arms — only 3-year EFS rates (77.6% vs 80.8%) and EFS event counts (37/182 vs 29/154). Per the synthesis plan, a hazard ratio must not be reconstructed from event counts or KM rates, so no HR/SE(logHR) is recorded; this row therefore cannot contribute an HR to the pooled analysis as reported. Additional caveat: adjuvant anthracycline (4xEC) was given optionally according to pCR status, so post-surgical treatment differed between arms.; excluded by outcome classification: does not match the requested outcome/timepoint (meta_analysis_candidate=False)
Publication Status: conference abstract (J Clin Oncol 36, 2018, suppl; abstr 573)
Participant type: Women with centrally confirmed triple-negative early breast cancer (ER/PR <1%, HER2-, cT1c-cT4c, cN0/+)
Outcome measurement: 3-year EFS rate (%) per arm and number of EFS events per arm; no hazard ratio or 95% CI reported
Outcome variable: Event-free survival (EFS), 3-year rate and EFS events
effect_direction: favours platinum (3y EFS 80.8% carboplatin vs 77.6% control), but no inferential test reported

Report_ID: Event-free survival (EFS), carboplatin vs no carboplatin (mITT)
Title: CALGB 40603 (Alliance): Long-Term Outcomes and Genomic Correlates of Response and Survival After Neoadjuvant Chemotherapy With or Without Carboplatin and Bevacizumab in Triple-Negative Breast Cancer
Author: Shepherd et al. (CALGB 40603 / Alliance)
Comment: Trial reports event-free survival (EFS), not DFS; EFS counts patients not undergoing surgery as having an event. Carboplatin effect is the marginal 2x2 factorial comparison (arms 3+4 vs 1+2), so the control group is shared with the bevacizumab comparison. Trial was not powered for EFS.
Design Type: randomized controlled trial (2x2 factorial, phase II)
Participant type: Women with clinical stage II-III triple-negative breast cancer
Outcome measurement: Cox proportional hazards model hazard ratio with 95% CI; log-rank P
Outcome variable: Event-free survival (EFS), carboplatin vs no carboplatin (mITT)
additional_group_ns: 2x2 factorial: bevacizumab yes n=222 / no n=221 (bevacizumab factor not extracted); by arm: arm 1 n=108, arm 2 n=110, arm 3 n=113, arm 4 n=112
effect_direction: slightly favours platinum but non-significant (HR 0.94, 95% CI 0.67-1.32)

Report_ID: Event-free survival (disease-free survival) — hazard ratio, DCb (carboplatin) vs EC-D (platinum-free)
Title: Neoadjuvant docetaxel plus carboplatin vs epirubicin plus cyclophosphamide followed by docetaxel in triple-negative, early-stage breast cancer (NeoCART): Results from a multicenter, randomized controlled, open-label phase II trial
Author: Zhang, Wu, Li, et al. (Wang K, corresponding)
Comment: HR is already oriented as platinum (DCb) vs platinum-free (EC-D), so no inversion needed. Note: the control arm is not the identical regimen minus platinum — EC-D is an anthracycline-containing backbone, while DCb is anthracycline-free; this is a regimen-substitution rather than a strict platinum add-on comparison. The reported CI is given with low precision (0.2-2.84). Group percentages are Kaplan-Meier 3-year EFS rates, not means.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('DCb group (docetaxel 75 mg/m2 + carboplatin AUC 6 q3w x 6 cycles) — platinum arm') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Design Type: randomized controlled trial (open-label, phase II, multicenter)
Participant type: Women with previously untreated stage II-III triple-negative breast cancer, ECOG 0-1, age >= 18
Recruitment source: Six participating centers in China (Guangdong Provincial People's Hospital and others), 1 Sep 2016 - 31 Dec 2019
Outcome measurement: Kaplan-Meier 3-year EFS rates and Cox hazard ratio with 95% CI and log-rank P value
Outcome variable: Event-free survival (disease-free survival) — hazard ratio, DCb (carboplatin) vs EC-D (platinum-free)

Title: Better pathologic complete response and relapse-free survival after carboplatin plus paclitaxel compared with epirubicin plus paclitaxel as neoadjuvant chemotherapy for locally advanced triple-negative breast cancer: a randomized phase 2 trial
Author: Zhang P, Yin Y, Mo H, et al.
Comment: The paper reports NO hazard ratio and NO 95% CI for RFS — only Kaplan-Meier curves, 1/3/5-year RFS rates, relapse event counts (9/47 vs 18/44) and a log-rank P = 0.043. Per the synthesis plan ("Do not rebuild a hazard ratio from event counts. If a paper reports only Kaplan-Meier curves and numbers at risk, leave the study out"), no HR was extracted or derived; event counts and the log-rank P are recorded verbatim only for auditability. Additional caveats: the control arm (EP) is an anthracycline-taxane regimen rather than the identical regimen minus platinum (PC is anthracycline-free), and 13 EP-arm patients crossed over to platinum-based adjuvant therapy after surgery.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('PC arm — paclitaxel 175 mg/m2 d1 + carboplatin AUC=5 d2, q3w x 4-6 cycles (platinum)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False); excluded by outcome classification: does not match the requested outcome/timepoint (meta_analysis_candidate=False)
Participant type: Women aged 18-75 with stage IIA-IIIC triple-negative invasive ductal breast cancer, ECOG 0-1, chemotherapy-naive
Recruitment source: Cancer Hospital, Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences and Peking Union Medical College (and Fujian Provincial Cancer Hospital), May 2006 - December 2012; NCT01276769
Outcome measurement: Kaplan-Meier 5-year RFS rate and relapse event counts; log-rank P value (no hazard ratio or 95% CI reported)
effect_direction: favours platinum (5-year RFS 77.6% vs 56.2%, log-rank P=0.043)
